goal_text: The chest is heavier than it looks. Behind you the caverns go quiet, as if they had been waiting to be solved.

lantern.name: oil lantern
lantern.description: A dented oil lantern. It still lights.

coin.name: silver coin
coin.description: A heavy silver coin stamped with a bridge.

camp.name: Cold Camp
camp.description: The ashes of a fire, a torn bedroll, a dripping ceiling. Whoever camped here left in a hurry. A wide passage leads north into the hill; a narrower one goes west, where you hear water.

cistern.name: Cistern
cistern.description: A round pool of black water fills the room from wall to wall. Nothing floats in it and nothing lies beside it. The only way is back east.

hall.name: Pillared Hall
hall.description: Six pillars hold up a ceiling you cannot see. To the north the hall ends in a tunnel that swallows all light; the air from it is cold and smells of deep stone. A low door stands west, a wide arch east, and the camp is south.

shrine.name: Shrine
shrine.description: A niche with a cracked statue of a seated figure. On the altar before it someone left an oil lantern. The door back east is the only exit.

gallery.name: Painted Gallery
gallery.description: Faded paintings of a procession cover the walls, all of them walking toward the floor at the far end, where the flagstones are newer than the rest and a thin draft rises between them. The arch back west is the only exit you can see.

down.reveal: You kneel where the painted figures point. One flagstone rocks under your hand; beneath it, steps lead down.

crypt.name: Crypt
crypt.description: Stone shelves hold the dead in neat rows. At the north end a bronze door shows a single carved footprint, and words run along its lintel. Steps lead back up.

north.riddle: The more of me you take, the more of me you leave behind. What am I?
north.closed: The lintel speaks the riddle. The bronze door stays shut.
north.opened: The carved footprint sinks into the bronze. The door opens.

vault.name: Toll Vault
vault.description: A small vault, empty but for a stone hand holding out a single silver coin stamped with a bridge. The door back south is the only way.

dark_tunnel.name: Dark Tunnel
dark_tunnel.description: Your light shows a tunnel cut through black rock, the floor split by a crevice you step across. Ahead, north, the tunnel opens onto a bridge, and from there comes slow, heavy breathing and the clink of a chain. South is the hall.
dark_tunnel.death: You walk into the dark with your hands out. The floor ends before your hands find anything.

bridge.name: Toll Bridge
bridge.description: A stone bridge over a drop you cannot see the bottom of, and on it a troll with a chain around one ankle and an open hand the size of a shield. He does not speak. He waits. North, past him, a landing; south, the tunnel.

hazard.pass: The troll closes his hand on the coin, bites it, and steps aside.
hazard.death: The troll's hand closes on you instead.

antechamber.name: Antechamber
antechamber.description: A square room with a door of green stone to the east, carved with coasts and rivers and tiny towers. Words are cut above it. The landing is back south.

east.riddle: I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, and water but no fish. What am I?
east.closed: The green door asks its question and does not move.
east.opened: The carved coasts slide apart. The door opens.

treasury.name: Treasury
treasury.description: A chest on a plinth, and nothing else.

landing.name: Landing of Two Arches
landing.description: A landing before two archways, east and west. Beyond each arch the floor is a painted cloth stretched over a shaft; you can see both cloths breathe in the draft, and a pebble dropped through either falls for a long time before it stops. One of the two cloths, the old story goes, lies over solid stone. Above the west arch a carved skull, above the east arch a carved cup. Letters cut into the step: THE SKULL KEEPS WHAT IT IS GIVEN. THE CUP GIVES IT BACK. The bridge is south.

oubliette.name: Oubliette
oubliette.death: The floor beyond the skull is a painted cloth over a shaft. The skull keeps you.
